svg.text: D — gauge-set, lock-held: original rim gauge and the rate-split branch (D-r / D-m), plan at the true opening pose
Tube and proxy gun to scale (grip 45, hole dial 30, vertical −15); gauge, foot pads, holder and stack placements are proposals.
dot
wire from −Y
D original: printed rim gauge (split, slides out
on +Y past the wire) receives the shell; kept as a pose CHECK
D-r foot (on the shell, 3 mm cam slide): Z pad on the
plate face r≈50, X pad on the bore; +Y side, 8 mm along
the seam (free side at this pose)
tacks (grey) while gauging: table indexed 22.5°, so the foot lands between tacks
holder base (lockable arm, D original;
in D-r the lead-screw slides hold)
stack: X slide, Y slide (yaw), recipe block
D original (wave 1)
one printed gauge on the rim sets all six freedoms per tube;
a single-lock holder holds; gauge removed before the weld.
Breaks: lock shift strains the gauge; the gauge must split
to pass the wire.
D-r (who-moves-what, wave 2)
split by rate: angles in a printed block (per recipe),
yaw/radial on lead-screw slides (per recipe; stopping
turning is locking), height per tube by the work,
set with the retractable foot.
D-m (who-moves-what)
a dial on the Z pad read at the eight between-tack angles:
the tube's runout map; set height to the mean.
Sequence (sequence-of-use)
index 22.5° → touch → read / set → retract → back to tack 1.
With the stand-hung plate head the foot only measures.
